findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the uploaded vendor roster) are stored without enforced KMS/SSE encryption.
No ACL is specified and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated, leaving the bucket without an explicit private posture or guard against a later public ACL/policy being applied.
The bucket holding report/vendor data has no logging block, so unauthorized access to its objects would leave no audit trail.
Versioning is not enabled, so object overwrite or deletion (including malicious tampering or ransomware) is unrecoverable; combined with force_destroy = true the data can be destroyed outright.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive financial export data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No versioning and no access logging are configured for the ledger bucket, so object tampering or deletion cannot be detected or recovered, and access to financial exports is not auditable.
Model artifact bucket configures versioning and logging but no server-side encryption default, leaving stored artifacts unencrypted.
Runbook bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration; operational runbooks frequently contain internal hostnames, procedures, and occasionally credentials, and are stored unencrypted.
No logging block is configured, so reads of runbook content are not recorded for audit or intrusion detection.

The ACL is set to "lcatalogopts-delivery-write", which is not a valid S3 canned ACL (the intended value is presumably log-delivery-write). A malformed grant on the central audit/log-destination bucket means log delivery and the intended access model are not applied as expected.

The bucket receiving access logs uses force_destroy = true and has no public access block or bucket policy restricting deletion, so audit evidence can be destroyed by a Terraform apply or an actor with bucket-level permissions.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party PII/business data) is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into a bucket that also lacks default encryption, so it is stored in cleartext.
